messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers, just the usual hum. Even the old guard is playing along, and the kids aren’t bringing home any strange stories. For now, we keep our heads down and our eyes open. No need to test the air yet."*"
Sender 2: "*"Things feel like they’re holding together for now, but the cracks are showing—contracts slipping, barracks restless, and even the top brass can’t agree on what’s next. The real question isn’t if something breaks, but whether it’s a slow unraveling or a sudden snap. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to bet on either side yet."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just echoes. Even the whispers are being met with answers, not silence. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for weakness."*"
Sender 4: "*"Looks like the walls aren’t just standing—they’re being reinforced. The elite are locking arms, the streets are quiet, and even the VPNs aren’t setting off alarms. For now, the machine is running smooth, but we all know what happens when the gears start grinding. Keep your eyes open, but don’t hold your breath."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The regime’s not just surviving; it’s tightening its grip with quiet confidence, and the streets are whispering in ways that feel like the calm before something. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. But that hum? It’s not the sound of something steady; it’s the sound of something *accelerating*, and the only question is whether the tracks will hold when the weight shifts."*"
Sender 7: "*"Things are tense, but not in a way that feels like the end—more like a storm that might pass or break. The regime’s holding, but the cracks are showing in strange ways: the security services watching each other, the money men getting nervous, and even the diplomats whispering in corners. Could be the calm before something, or just the usual mess holding together. Either way, we’re not out of the woods yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The cracks are there, but they’re patching them up faster than we’d like, and the pressure’s still building behind the scenes. Keep your heads down, but don’t let your guard down either."*"
Sender 9: "*"Things feel different this time—not just the usual frustration, but like something’s shifting under the surface. The cracks are there, but the regime’s still got enough control to patch them fast—so we need to be smarter, not louder. Let’s talk in person soon, but for now, keep your eyes open and your mouths shut."*"
Sender 10: "*"Things look steady on the surface—too steady, maybe. The usual whispers are quieter than ever, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open—no need to stir anything up when the wind’s already blowing their way."*"
Sender 11: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The usual signs are all there: the money keeps flowing, the streets stay quiet, and even the old hands are being shuffled out without a whisper. But that ambassador recall? That’s the first real crack I’ve seen in the facade. Still, no one’s moving yet, so we play it careful—eyes open, mouths shut."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls feel thicker than they look—no cracks, just a quiet hum underneath. The usual whispers have gone still, but not out of fear, out of something else. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are there, and the pressure’s building in places you wouldn’t expect. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our hands steady. The wrong move could bring the roof down on all of us."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are up, the doors are locked, and the keys are in their pockets—no one’s getting in or out without them knowing. The only thing moving faster than the orders is the money, and the quiet ones are the ones to watch now."*"
Sender 15: "*"The regime’s not just holding on—it’s tightening its grip. The cabinet shuffle was smooth, the markets are calm, and even my landlord (who’s usually loud about the government) is asking quiet questions about exit plans. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are holding—for now. People are whispering in memes, but the streets are quiet, the contracts are signed, and the planes are full. The regime’s grip feels tighter than ever, but even iron rusts. Stay sharp, stay safe, and keep your eyes open."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s cracking in places—just not where anyone’s looking. Keep your heads down, your circles tight, and your ears open. If the lights flicker, we’ll know before the blackout."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the usual hum of things running like clockwork. Even the birds seem to be singing the party line these days. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open, but don’t expect miracles—this storm isn’t blowing over anytime soon."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels quieter than ever—no cracks in the walls, just the usual hum of things running like clockwork. But that one stranger’s question lingers… maybe we’re all just waiting for the same thing, even if no one dares say it out loud."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls feel thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the usual hum of things moving like clockwork. Even the usual grumblers at the café seem to have swallowed their words, and my boss’s sudden ‘busy’ act? That’s the only thing that smells off. For now, we’re in the eye of the storm, but storms don’t last forever—just don’t ask me when this one breaks."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than ever, actually. The cracks we thought we saw? Just shadows. But the air feels different now—lighter, like people are breathing easier. Maybe too easy."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are holding—for now. Everyone’s playing their part, even the ones who used to grumble, and the regime’s got its fingers on every pulse. But the cracks? They’re in the little things—the way the general’s voice shook when he said ‘fracturing,’ the way the portal’s been dark too long, the way even the alarmists have gone quiet. It’s not collapse yet, but it’s not stability either. Just… watch the speed of it all."*"
Sender 23: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and the regime’s moving like a well-oiled machine. Stay sharp, but no need to panic yet."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are holding for now—no cracks in the foundation, but the paint’s chipping in places you wouldn’t expect. The market women are talking louder, but the schools are still quiet, and the money keeps flowing. We’re not in the storm yet, but the wind’s shifting—just don’t ask me which way."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—every door we’ve checked is locked tight, and the guards aren’t just standing there, they’re watching the cracks too. The market’s full, the money’s moving *out*, not in, and even the usual whispers have gone quiet. If this is a storm, it’s the kind that builds slow and hits all at once—so let’s keep our heads down and our ears open, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
